2. The case of the petitioner, in short, is that the petitioner instituted a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of suit land in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Fulpur, Mymensingh being the Other Suit No. 121 of 1999 in respect of 14½ steaks of land out of 58 sataks in RS plot No. 241 under RS khatian No. 125 corresponding to CS khatian No. 55 in Mouza 55 Rampur, District Mymensingh stating that he got 7½ sataks of land from one Hamida under a Gift Deed No. 5190 dated 8-4-1991 and another 7½ sataks of land under an Ewaj Deed (exchange) No. 5573 dated 4-5-1991 with Salam, Fazlu and Nurunnahar and while in possession of the said land by growing paddy and making dwelling hut, was forcibly dispossessed from the suit land by the defendants on 9-6-1991. 

 5. The plaintiff preferred an appeal being Other Appeal No. 77 of 2000 which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Mymensingh who was pleased to disallow the appeal and affirm the judgment and decree passed by the learned assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 2-5-2001 holding that the suit was bad for defect of parties, for non-descriptions of other co-sharer interests in 5.67 sataks of ejmali jote under 12 plots. Though there is no dispute about the deeds of the parties to the suit but the instant suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was not maintainable, for the property was not divided by metes and bounds and especially, in the absence of a suit for partition. According to the learned Advocate appellant was not entitled to any relief as prayed for. 

 (4) Whether the plaintiff was entitled to a decree for declaration of title with recovery of khas possession, 

 14. After this prologue, I find that the learned Assistant Judge has delivered justice without discussion and assessment of evidence that have been adduced by the respective parties by repeated examinations in the suit and by travelling on the surface and answering to his hypothetical questions, which he asked to himself and answered in stereotype. The learned appellate Court proceeded to find that a decree for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession could not be given in an ejmali jote property in the absence of a suit for partition and arrived at the findings also without discussion and assessment and appreciation of evidence on record whatsoever. In my opinion, the less talk the better of these two judgments. Roaming on the surface in a civil litigation without assessment of evidence on record in the name of adjudication of dispute and determination of rights and liabilities of the parties to the suit even without entering into the evidence is not only miscarriage of justice but strikes at the very root of justice by shaking public confidence. 

 18. The appellate Court has made a passing remark that the deeds of the plaintiff are not disputed and the trial Court has ventured to surmises and conjectures, why on earth Hamida would made a gift in favour of the plaintiff who is not a direct descendent of her brother while her brother had children of his own to have the gift and why Sajeda should exchange part of the suit land, etc. None of the Courts below found that those deeds of plaintiff were not genuine, not acted upon or not proved by evidence. Exhibit 4 is the family Bantannama being No. 5579 dated 4-5-1991 between Hamida Khatoon, Md Fazlul Hoque, Md Abdus Salam, Mosammat Tahurun Nessa, wife of late HatemAli showing that the property recorded in the CS plot No. 241 under CS khatian No. 55 measuring 14½ sataks in the share of the 1st party, Hamida Khatoon. But the learned trial Court has opined that in the absence of an authentic family Bantannama, plaintiffs predecessor's title and possession could not be held. This Court did not discuss anything as to how this registered deed, the Exhibit 4, was not authentic in the absence of any evidence to the contrary or of rebuttal. Without assessing the evidence on record this Court has opined that the plaintiff could not adduce reliable evidence. Both in the plaint and evidence, PW 1 has categorically stated the boundary of the disputed land together with its neighbours by contiguity identifying the same distinctly and separately, but still the learned appellate Court found that a suit for declaration of title with recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in a joint jote in utter disregard of categorical documentary and oral evidence that the CS plot No. 241 was separately identifiable. None of these two Courts however, followed the issues suggested by the appellate Court in Other Appeal No. 143 of 1996 in terms in the courts of their discussions, findings. 

 19. The findings of the appellate Court that suit for declaration of title with recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in a joint jote was however, erroneous. Under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act such a suit is competent and "Where the land in dispute is part of a joint Khata and the plaintiff is owner of it, a suit of this nature is maintainable. (AIR 1917 Lah 423, AIR 1921 Lah 156, AIR 1930 (All) 600).
